correctness.rationale: The printed x2 equation gives the rigorous upper inequality x2' <= (B+rb)x2 because x1/(k2+x1)<1 and the quadratic term is nonpositive. Combining it with the impulse produces an exact geometric upper bound when q=(1-omega)exp((B+rb)T)<1. At q=1, the independent logistic upper bound for x1 makes the gain strictly less than rb eventually, again forcing decay. The counterexample satisfies every condition explicitly listed in Theorem 3.8, as checked algebraically from the source definitions, while q<1 forces x2 to zero.

value.rationale: The source uses Theorem 3.8 to identify fishery regimes in which both populations persist. The counterexample shows that its listed conditions can instead force the economically central short-mackerel population to extinction, even while retaining the paper's own biological parameters. The necessary pulse-survival inequality is simple, model-intrinsic, and directly constrains any corrected management threshold.
